QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_13

question.text: As per Ch 9, the typical upper cap on one-time Set-up Costs charged by the Investment Manager to an AIF's investors is:

answer.text: No cap — set-up costs are borne actuals

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Ch 9.1: Set-up costs can go up to 1.5% or 2.5% of total capital commitments raised, amortized over 36 months or the fund life from First Close. **The Trap:** Option A is egregiously high. Option C is absurd. Option D confuses set-up with Transaction Expenses (which are on actuals without limit). **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A/B tests the cap; XIX-C tests the amortisation mechanic. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Always spell out amortisation method in the PPM (straight-line over 36 months vs over fund life). Some LPs prefer front-loaded amortisation so late-cycle entrants via subsequent closes don't bear disproportionate set-up costs.
